newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Ex-Islamist party in Algeria threatens poll pullout.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Islamist party in Algeria threatens poll pullout.

text.p: Algeria's main legal Islamist- leaning party on Monday threatened to withrdaw from the country's June 5 parliamentary election if the government did not stop an alleged campaign of "lies" against its leader.

"If we find out that this intensive bombardment of lies is not stopped and if the president of the republic did not intervene to stop this bombardment...we will withdraw from the elections," Mahfoud Nahnah, leader of the Movement of a Peaceful Society (MPS), told a news conference in Algiers.

Nahnah, who won one third of the vote in the 1995 plural presidential elections which returned President Liamine Zeroual to power, was reacting to statements by supporters and allies of the president branding Nahnah a "former Islamist terrorist".
Zeroual's supporters also accused the veteran Islamist leader of using the Moslem faith as a tool to win votes in the elections to the 380-seat National Assembly.

Nahnah changed the name of his party in April in line with a new law banning political parties based on Islam. The former Movement of the Islamic Society -- known by its Arabic acronym Hamas -- became Movement of a Peaceful Society.

MPS, which plans to field candidates in 52 of Algeria's 56 overall constituencies, is seen by many independent pundits as the main contender in the poll pitting more than 7,000 candidates from 39 political parties and hundreds of independents.
The June 5 general election is the first since the authorities cancelled in 1992 a poll in which radical Islamists took a huge lead.
About 60,000 people have been killed in violence pitting Moslem rebels against government forces since.
